title: Target Circuit Matching in Large-Scale Netlists Using GNN-Based Region Prediction
problem: Subgraph matching in circuit verification struggles with large-scale circuits; traditional rule-based methods lack generalization, and node-to-node approaches are computationally inefficient.
motivation: Efficient subgraph matching enables faster circuit verification and design exploration for large chips.
method: The approach uses a Graph Neural Network (an AI trained on interconnected data) to predict which regions of a large circuit netlist (the description of how electronic components connect) are likely to contain the target circuit pattern. It trains using both positive examples of real matches and negative samples (similar-looking non-matches) so the model learns to tell them apart accurately. Rather than running the neural network separately for every possible location in the circuit—which is computationally expensive—the method directly extracts numerical representations of circuit patterns that capture the whole circuit's structure at once. This filters the search down to the most promising regions before doing expensive detailed matching on individual candidates.
key_novelty: It predicts which regions of the circuit likely contain the target pattern first using a neural network, then applies detailed matching only to those regions instead of checking every location.
contributions: GNN-based target region prediction eliminating per-candidate subgraph matching
Negative sample construction for accurate circuit detection
Direct subgraph embedding extraction capturing global circuit information
Significantly outperforms existing methods in time efficiency and prediction accuracy

metrics.method: time efficiency and region prediction accuracy

limitations: Evaluation details sparse in abstract; specific benchmark sets and comparison metrics not fully specified.
primary_theme: GNN-based efficient subgraph matching for circuit verification
